I farm 10.9 mu, so I am not too small and not too big. I still count every bag, because if I spend too much on fertilizer, then I get tight on spray money and machine work. I usually start from what I did last year, then change a little if I think it will pay. Here in Quzhou, with well irrigation, wheat and maize can both give good yield if I do not let fertilizer and water fall short. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too complicated. I look at my own field, what the neighbors are doing, and what gave steady harvest before. For wheat, I will keep an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer, water about 3 times, and spray 3 times because rust, aphids, and later disease can hurt yield fast. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because around here it yields better and stands better. Maize is after wheat, so time is tight. I will do simple tillage, keep fertilizer a little strong, water 2 times if rain is not enough, and spray 2 times mainly for weeds and insects. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. On this land, with water from the well, I will aim for a stable wheat-maize double crop and not take big risks.
